verification.content_review: Both: employers and workers must adhere to Sharia when applying the Law.

Both: incidental, seasonal and temporary workers are subject to the same 9 listed areas (duties and discipline; maximum hours; daily/weekly rest; overtime; official holidays; safety rules; occupational health; work injuries and compensation; Minister's decisions). All 9 present on both sides.

Both: clause 1 Saudization duties (attract, employ, retain, guide/train/qualify); clause 2 Saudi workers at least 75% of the workforce; Minister may reduce the share temporarily when qualified nationals are unavailable.

Both: an employer must re-employ a worker whose work injury reduces capacity but permits other work, in a suitable job at that job's wage; injury compensation is preserved. Nuance: EN 'another job' leaves implicit the AR 'other than his previous work'.
Both: recruitment from abroad for work requires Ministry approval.
Both: no employment outside the profession on the work permit; worker may not change profession before legal procedures.
Both: defines the qualification/training contract binding the employer to prepare a person for a specific profession. Nuance: AR 'qualify or train', EN 'train and qualify'.

Both: training contract subject to 7 listed areas (annual leave; official holidays; maximum hours; daily/weekly rest; occupational safety and health; work injuries and conditions; Minister's decisions).
Both: monthly-paid worker may not be moved to daily/weekly/piecework/hourly pay without written consent; acquired rights preserved.
Both: worker duties beyond the Law - six numbered items (work per instructions; care of employer property; conduct; help in disasters without extra pay; medical examinations; confidentiality).

Both: no penalty for off-site acts unless work-related; fine per violation max five days' wage; one penalty per violation; deductions max five days' wage per month; unpaid suspension max five days per month.
Both: Council of Ministers may set a minimum wage on the Minister's proposal.

Both: no deductions without written consent except six numbered cases (10% loan cap; social insurance; savings fund; housing scheme; fines/damages; court judgment capped at one quarter), with alimony first.

Both: Articles 98 and 101 do not apply to four numbered cases (senior management; preparatory/supplementary work; intermittent work; guards and cleaners except civil security guards); Regulations set jobs and maximum hours for items 2-4.
Both: Minister issues rules for part-time work; the Law applies only as the Minister decides, except occupational safety/health and work-injury protection.
Both: this Chapter does not cover establishments that fall under the occupational-hazards branch of social insurance.
Both: work injury as defined by the Social Insurance Law; occupational diseases count as work injuries; date of first medical diagnosis counts as the injury date.

Both: permanent total disability or death gives compensation of 3 years' wages with a 54,000-riyal minimum (AR in words); partial disability gives the assessed percentage per the approved disability guide times the total-disability amount.
Both: after maternity leave, nursing break(s) totalling at most 1 hour per day, in addition to general rest periods, counted as working time, with no wage reduction.
Both: in all occupations and places employing women, the employer provides seats for their rest.
Both: minors barred from hazardous or harmful work endangering health, safety or morals; the Minister specifies such work by decision.

Both: clause 1 minimum age 15 (Minister may raise it); clause 2 exception for ages 13-15 in light work subject to sub-clauses 2/1 (EN 2.1) no harm to health or growth and 2/2 (EN 2.2) no hindrance to schooling or training.
Both: minors may not work during a night period of at least 12 consecutive hours (AR in words), except as the Minister decides.
Both: actual underground work at most 7 hours per day; presence at the workplace at most 10 hours per day (AR in words), including underground travel time.
Both: the employer or responsible manager issues a list of public-safety orders and instructions.
Both: inspector may order changes to equipment/machinery operating rules within set deadlines for health and safety, and may require immediate measures against an imminent hazard.
Both: inspector keeps complaints about equipment shortages or violations absolutely confidential and must not reveal their existence to the employer or representative.

Both: physicians, engineers, chemists and occupational safety and health specialists join inspections as needed; labor office director and inspectors may ask competent executive bodies for assistance.
Both: supersedes the Labor and Workers Law (Royal Decree M/21 dated 6/9/1389H); repeals conflicting provisions; earlier regulations remain until amended.
Both: published in the Official Gazette; in force 180 days after publication (AR in words).

review_provenance.agent_review: Claude (AI agent, claude-opus-5-5), 2026-11-23: side-by-side reading of every extracted Arabic/English pair, checking numbered clauses and sub-clauses, enumerated lists, exceptions, numbers, percentages, dates and legal references.
automated_checks: existing eligibility rule (no amendment recorded in either source; unique, non-bis, nonempty)
every digit sequence in the Arabic text also occurs in the English text
English text is an exact substring of an independent extractor's output (poppler pdftotext, whitespace-normalized)
run-time token-count guards (no truncation/padding, full character coverage, no special/unknown ids)
review_provenance.human_approval: PENDING: no human has reviewed or approved any pair in this corpus (including the 10 pilot pairs)
review_provenance.pilot_notes: notes for the 10 pilot articles are carried over unchanged from manifest/review.json

procedure: Pool: pairs passing the existing eligibility rule, minus the 10 pilot articles
Excluded from pool: Part 11 (marine terms redefined by M/44) and articles mentioning the Labor Dispute Commissions (M/1 global phrase replacement)
Strata: pool sorted by Arabic character count (ties by article number) and cut into thirds
Quotas 7 short / 7 medium / 6 long; within a stratum, repeatedly take the candidate whose Part has the fewest selected articles (pilot included), ties broken by SHA-256(seed:article)
Token counts are never consulted during selection
